title: Pre-Analysis — Frame Foot Renewal and Bilge Treatment Aft of Frame 62 on the Four-Engine Aircraft
abstract: Original pre-analysis for the renewal of corroded frame feet and the re-treatment of the bilge between frame 62 and the rear pressure bulkhead on four-engine aircraft, closed with conditions on the repaired population.

sections.objective: Establish what the proposed frame foot renewal and bilge re-treatment aft of frame 62 would disturb on the four-engine aircraft, where the aft galley complex and the extended crew rest raise the local moisture load. The work order had to establish the repaired population in the target area, confirm the protective scheme is consistent with the standard already adopted further forward, and record whether any external repair interacts with internal renewal in the same bay.
sections.findings_summary: The dominant result is the repair population. The approved blend-out and spliced renewal scheme is already carried by a meaningful share of the target fleet, and the proposed work installs new material and a new fastener pattern over exactly the splice fastener rows the repair puts under repeat inspection; neither the life limit nor the inspection survives the renewal as written. The parts figure covers the same frame and foot family and today has no way of expressing two renewal standards on the same item. The external patch repair below the cargo floor line was the surprise: it shares two zones with the proposed work and describes the same bay from outside, and a combined internal and external stack has never been substantiated. The protective scheme itself is consistent with the standard adopted at the forward door surround, which removes one open question rather than adding one.
sections.next_steps: Obtain a repair design position on whether a spliced foot may be over-worked or must be cut out to sound material, and add a pre-embodiment repair survey to the retrofit bulletin. Ask the illustrated parts owner for a renewal variant on the frame foot family. Refer the combined internal and external stack to structures certification before the design review rather than after it. Record the protective scheme alignment in the dossier so that the next section does not re-open it.

similarity_seeds: exfoliation at frame feet under an aft galley complex
corrosion inhibiting compound re-applied over a dried bilge

tasks.title: Size the repaired population in the target bay
Search external repairs on the same lower shell bay
Confirm protective scheme alignment with the forward standard
Review the frame foot parts family for a renewal variant

evidence.similarity_note: Both methods return it: the fastener standard is common and the two texts describe the same frame foot material loss condition in almost the same words.

expected_findings.rationale: A spliced foot carries a life limit and a repeat eddy current inspection of the splice fastener rows. The renewal installs new material and a new fastener pattern over those rows, which makes the recorded limit untraceable and the inspection impossible to perform as written.
expected_findings.resolution: Obtain a repair design position and add a pre-embodiment repair survey to the retrofit bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries the frame and foot family for the whole bilge area with no way to express two renewal standards on the same item. The renewal items and the original items are not interchangeable and would be ordered against the same description.
expected_findings.resolution: Request a renewal variant with its own effectivity on the frame foot family.

expected_findings.rationale: The external patch repair sits on the lower shell of the same bay, below the cargo floor line. An aircraft carrying the patch and then receiving the internal renewal ends with a stack that neither substantiation covers, and the patch perimeter inspection is not accounted for by the renewal.
expected_findings.resolution: Refer the combined stack to structures certification before design review.

evidence.similarity_note: No shared identifier. The link is the protective scheme: both adopt the same chromate-free primer and drainage philosophy, one at a forward door surround and one at an aft bilge, and the two texts have almost no vocabulary in common.

expected_findings.rationale: The forward standard fixed the protective scheme the fleet now uses on lower shell frame feet. Confirming alignment removes an open question rather than adding one, and it means the two areas can share a single acceptance criterion.
expected_findings.resolution: Record the alignment in the dossier; no design or applicability action.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the aft equipment zone and is returned by any zone-driven search over this bay. It is a pneumatic valve internal change with no structural, protective or drainage content, and nothing it installs sits on the frame feet.

type_data.conclusion: The renewal is sound. Conditions attach on the spliced repair population, the parts family variant and the combined external patch stack.
